trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or around the edge to (1,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going around the edge to (1,5) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes around the edge to (5,1).
I can't rule out right or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going around the edge to (1,2) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,3); going to number 3, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (right from cell (5,1)) was wrong, so the line must go up.
The line must go right: up is number 5, which comes later; around the edge to (4,5) is number 9, which comes later.
Going up would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going right would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes down.
The line must go left: around the edge to (1,3) is number 7, which comes later.
Going right would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4). So the line goes left.
Going around the edge to (2,5) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Cell (3,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would strand number 7: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right would wall in number 10, the last number. So the line goes down.
Going right would cut off the top edge (2 cells). So the line goes down.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 23 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 11/25 cells (44%).
Generation 1: fitness 25/25. The best line covers 25 cells.
Generation 1: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 72 futures: 96% survive going right (best covers 44%); around the edge to (1,4) 92%; up 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 100% survive going around the edge to (5,1) (best covers 44%); around the edge to (1,5) 92%.
Tried 48 futures: 79% survive going up (best covers 32%); right 67%.
Jackpot! A future after going right covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 25 cells x 25 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
